- Young soybean seedlings in pots
- Large lower leaves show prominent **white/pale powdery patches** on the upper surface
- Upper younger leaves appear more normal green
- No obvious lesions with dark margins, no angular spots

Top candidates: **Powdery_Mildew** (white powdery growth on upper leaf surface), possibly Downy_mildew or Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus. Let me view reference images.

None of the other candidates match. All confirm the diagnosis:

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: Young potted soybean seedlings with **prominent white/gray powdery patches on the upper surface of lower leaves**
- Upper younger leaves appear normal green — disease is progressing from lower canopy upward
- No angular spots, no dark margins, no lesions with halos, no vein-following patterns, no stem lesions

**Powdery Mildew** reference collage shows exactly this: white to gray powdery fungal growth coating the upper leaf surface, particularly on lower/older leaves. The symptom description matches perfectly: "white, powdery fungal growth that can cover all aboveground plant parts, particularly the upper leaf surface."

All other candidates clearly don't fit — Cercospora shows dark purple coloration, Downy mildew shows mottled yellowish spots, Bacterial Blight shows angular water-soaked lesions, stem diseases show root/stem symptoms not leaf coating.
